chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Abi Umayr from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)
Regarding a person in ihram who was affected by perfume, he said: 'There is no harm if he wipes it off with his hand or washes it.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah will surely test you with some game that your hands and spears shall attain.' He said: 'The game was gathered for them from every direction until it drew near to them to test them with it.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the person in ihram should not use black kohl (al-sawad), but he may use kohl made from sabr and haddad, and what resembles them, if he wishes.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.السَّوَاد: Black kohl (specifically the type made from a specific plant, often considered prohibited for muhrim)
key_terms.الصَّبِر: A type of plant used for kohl, permissible for muhrim
key_terms.الْحُضُض: A type of plant used for kohl, permissible for muhrim

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a pilgrim in ihram regarding perfume and eye kohl?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of a muhrim removing or washing off perfume, distinguishing it from the prohibition of consuming it. It provides a specific exegetical insight into Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:94, explaining that the 'test' of hunting involved game being gathered around the pilgrims to make the trial immediate and tangible. Additionally, Sheikh al-Tusi notes the juristic distinction between prohibited black kohl and permissible natural alternatives like sabr and haddad, reflecting the practical legal reasoning of the Ahl al-Bayt.
